title: Import Patterns from File: the imported stitches land centred on the Design Page
description: PE-DESIGN 11.50's Import Patterns > from File ignores where the file put its stitches and centres the pattern on the Design Page, for a DST and a PES alike, on a 100 x 100 and a 200 x 150 mm page; importing the same file twice puts the copies on top of each other. The source is an OpenStitch export of a 20 x 10 mm rectangle at (10,10) mm. One stitch more in PE's double import (785 against 784: PE joins the copies with a stitch where OpenStitch jumps) is inside the count tolerance; the DST's colour (PE: 007 PRUSSIAN BLUE) is not compared.

featureMatrix.feature: Import stitch files into the design

evidence.note: compat/reference/stitches/import-*.pes (PE-DESIGN 11.50, 2026-10-31, pe-refs-4 round 7): every import centred on the page

references.make: App menu > New (Hoop 100 x 100 mm); Home > Import Patterns > from File... (opens the Import pane: From Folder, File Type filter, thumbnails; no dialog or option at import), the source's thumbnail > Import for import-rect20x10.dst; Save As PES (default type, #PES0110)

App menu > New (Hoop 100 x 100 mm); Home > Import Patterns > from File... (opens the Import pane: From Folder, File Type filter, thumbnails; no dialog or option at import), the source's thumbnail > Import for import-rect20x10.pes; Save As PES (default type, #PES0110)

App menu > New (Hoop 100 x 100 mm); Home > Import Patterns > from File... (opens the Import pane: From Folder, File Type filter, thumbnails; no dialog or option at import), the source's thumbnail > Import for import-rect20x10.dst, then the same Import again; Save As PES (default type, #PES0110)

App menu > New, Design Page Custom 200 x 150 mm; Home > Import Patterns > from File... (opens the Import pane: From Folder, File Type filter, thumbnails; no dialog or option at import), the source's thumbnail > Import for import-rect20x10.dst; Save As PES (default type, #PES0110)

PE-DESIGN 11.50's canvas and rulers put this import at 40 mm; its file cannot show it: on the 100 x 100 mm page PE-DESIGN writes these PEC stitches from the design's own top-left (PEC header 20,0 x 10,0 mm, needle points 0-20 x 0-10 mm), where its 200 x 150 mm file and its other 100 x 100 references (header 2900 x 1900) keep page coordinates. A machine reads both the same way. This check pins OpenStitch's page position at PE's ruler value.
